title: Session Evacuation and Eviction Protocol Spec
author: Priya Shah
content:
Overview
--------
This design specification defines the Session Evacuation and Eviction Protocol (SEEP), a deterministic runtime policy and associated control plane/agent contracts for moving or terminating conversational sessions when physical or logical serving capacity changes. SEEP ensures customer-facing session continuity goals are balanced with infrastructure safety, cost controls, and predictable developer-facing semantics.

Motivation and goals
--------------------
- Reduce user-visible errors (Partial responses, broken websockets, abruptly ended sessions) during planned maintenance, scaling events, or overloaded nodes.
- Provide deterministic, testable behaviors for session takeover, graceful evacuation, and controlled eviction.
- Define a telemetry contract so downstream product and SRE teams can evaluate impact to SLAs and unit economics.
- Keep developer surface minimal: a small set of statuses and webhooks/streaming events that SDKs can observe and act on.

Scope and non-goals
-------------------
In-scope:
- Real-time conversational session evacuation and eviction for hosted and dedicated deployments.
- Node-initiated evacuation (drain + migrate), controller-initiated evacuation (region failover), and aggressive eviction for capacity emergency.
- Telemetry and observability signals needed for SLOs and billing reconciliation.

Out-of-scope:
- Long-running offline batch migration of embeddings/long-term KV stores (handled by cache lifecycle team).
- Application-level retry logic (consumer SDKs should use the provided events; app-specific retry strategies are not prescribed here).

Key concepts and definitions
----------------------------
- Session: a conversational context with a session_id and associated KV/decoder state stored in the session-store and optionally in node-local KV cache.
- Evacuation: proactive process where a node coordinates moving an active session to another node and updating routing state so new requests are routed correctly.
- Eviction: forced termination of a session when no migration path is available or policy prefers termination (cost/priority/tenancy).
- Drain window: configured time budget for graceful evacuation (default 8s for low-latency, 30s for long-running sessions).
- Priority hints: tenant metadata used to select which sessions to keep when resources are constrained (e.g., enterprise tier, SLA tags).

High-level architecture
-----------------------
Services and components referenced in this spec:
- router-service: global request router; maintains mapping of session_id -> node_id and handles route changes.
- session-agent (node-local): manages KV cache, in-flight token emission, and coordinates evacuation/eviction with the controller.
- evacuation-coordinator: control-plane controller that orchestrates drain, migration, and final state transitions.
- session-store: durable store for session canonical state (cold copy) and migration journal.
- telemetry-proxy: funnel for structured telemetry events (metrics, traces, structured logs) from session-agent and coordinator.

Event sequence diagrams (text)
----------------------------
1) Planned node maintenance (drain)
- operator triggers maintenance -> evacuation-coordinator marks node_id as DRAINING.
- evacuation-coordinator requests router-service to stop new allocations to node_id and to return list of active sessions (streaming).
- session-agent receives DRAIN signal and begins per-session evacuation in parallel, honoring priority hints.
- For each session: session-agent writes migration intent to session-store, streams session-state to target node(s) using the migration API, updates router-service with new mapping when migration ACK returned.
- Once all sessions are migrated or drain-window expires, node marks DRAIN_COMPLETE and controller moves node to maintenance.

2) Emergency eviction (capacity pressure)
- Node under severe memory/CPU pressure triggers local eviction policy.
- session-agent evaluates eviction candidates by (priority -> last-active -> estimated cost-to-migrate).
- For selected sessions: session-agent emits 'eviction.advised' event to telemetry-proxy, then attempts a fast checkpoint to session-store. If checkpoint fails or cost>threshold, session_agent emits 'eviction.forced' and transitions session to TERMINATED with reason code.

Policy model and decision graph
------------------------------
Policy inputs (ordered by precedence):
1. Regional controller emergency flag (highest precedence).
2. Tenant priority hint (enterprise > paid > freemium).
3. Session SLA tag (e.g., response-consistency-sla: 99.5%).
4. Session idle-time and recent token-rate.
5. Estimated migration cost (bytes to transfer + deserialization cost).

Decision outcomes:
- MIGRATE -> attempt graceful transfer to target node (preferred).
- STALL -> permit the current node to finish tokens but block new requests (used during short drains).
- TERMINATE -> close the session and persist the terminal marker (eviction).

API contract: session-agent <-> evacuation-coordinator (HTTP + streaming)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
- POST /v1/nodes/{node_id}/evacuate  (controller -> node): triggers drain, body: {"drain_window_s":<int>, "policy_override": <string|null>}
- GET /v1/nodes/{node_id}/sessions?status=active (controller -> router-service): streaming list of session_id, priority, last_active, size_bytes
- POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/migrate (agent -> controller/target): body: { "target_node": "node-99", "checkpoint_uri": "s3://sessions/...", "mode": "copy|move" }
- POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/terminate (agent -> controller): body: { "reason": "eviction_forced|evacuation_timeout|policy_terminate", "user_visible_msg": "optional" }

Configuration table (defaults and allowed ranges)
------------------------------------------------
| key | default | valid values | description |
|----|---------:|--------------|------------|
| session.eviction.drain_window_s | "8" | "1..300" | Graceful drain time per node for low-latency clusters.
| session.eviction.max_concurrent_migrations | "32" | "1..500" | Max parallel migrations a node can attempt.
| session.eviction.priority_weights | "enterprise:100,paid:60,free:10" | comma-separated weights | Weighting for selection.
| session.eviction.fast_checkpoint_threshold_bytes | "1_048_576" | bytes | Sessions larger than this will prefer MIGRATE with snapshot vs inline transfer.

SLOs and thresholds
-------------------
- Migration success rate: >= 99.5% for planned drains (measured over daily windows).
- User-visible abrupt-termination rate due to evacuation: <= 0.05% of active session starts per month.
- Average additional tail latency introduced by evacuation activities: <= 5ms p95.

Telemetry and observability contract
----------------------------------
All session-agent and evacuation-coordinator events MUST be emitted to telemetry-proxy with the following minimal structured schema (JSON log):
- event.type (string): one of ["evacuation.start","session.migrate.attempt","session.migrate.success","session.migrate.fail","session.evict.advised","session.evict.forced","evacuation.complete","evacuation.timeout"]
- event.ts (ISO8601)
- node.id, session.id, tenant.id
- reason_code (if applicable)
- estimated_migration_bytes, actual_migration_bytes
- migration_duration_ms
- outcome (migrated|terminated|stalled|failed)

Metrics (prometheus counters/gauges) to be emitted by session-agent:
- seep_migrations_total{outcome="success|fail|partial"} (counter)
- seep_evictions_total{reason="policy|emergency|quota"} (counter)
- seep_migration_duration_seconds (histogram)
- seep_migration_queue_length (gauge)

Alerting and dashboards
- Pager alert: seep_migrations_total{outcome="fail"} rate > 1% over 15m => P1 to runtime-sre.
- Dashboard: per-tenant migration success rate, per-region drain completion latency histogram, and eviction counts by reason.

Operator runbook (high level)
----------------------------
1. Planned maintenance: trigger controller API -> verify router-service stops new allocations -> monitor seep_migration_queue_length and migration success events.
2. If migration failures spike: abort remaining migrations and mark node for emergency evacuation with policy_override: "suppress-migration" to avoid cascading failures.
3. If user-visible termination breaches SLO: initiate retrospective (ticket), enable increased drain_window for the affected cluster, and schedule canary maintenance.

Rollout and migration plan
-------------------------
- Canary (stage): implement protocol in dev cluster; run 10% of internal traffic with drain_window=30s for 2 weeks. Run synthetic churn tests with the migration harness.
- Beta (staging): enable in staging and run an 8-week soak with tenant-priority simulation (mix matching enterprise/freemium ratios).
- GA (hosted): default drain_window=8s for low-latency clusters; allow per-tenant overrides for Dedicated customers via account settings.

Backward compatibility and SDK guidance
--------------------------------------
- SDKs should handle the following session status codes sent over streaming: ACTIVE, DRAINING, MIGRATING, TERMINATED.
- On MIGRATING, SDKs MUST retry open requests within 500ms and reconnect using the session_id; router-service should direct to new node.
- Applications that require absolute continuity (no replays) should mark sessions with "persistence: true" and will be placed in a protected priority bucket (note: larger migration cost).

Testing matrix
--------------
1. Unit tests: policy decision graph permutations with mocked inputs.
2. Integration tests: controller + router + two node session_agent migration flows (happy and failure paths).
3. Chaos test: random node kill during migration and verify migration journal recovery (target success rate >= 99%).
4. Load test: synthetic churn at 5x peak expected tenant churn. Validate migration queue length and p95 migration_duration under threshold.

Security and compliance considerations
-------------------------------------
- Migration checkpoints and snapshots MUST be encrypted at rest (KMS-managed keys) and signed for integrity.
- Evacuation events with tenant metadata are considered sensitive and are routed through the telemetry-proxy with access controls; PII must be redacted before emission.

Ownership and maintenance
------------------------
- Feature owner: Priya Shah (serving-runtime).
- Primary review/approver: Daniel Kim (runtime-sre).
- Runtime implementation: eng-serving-runtime/session-agent team.
- Observability and alerts: eng-platform/dashboards team.

Appendix: sample migration request (YAML)
--------------------------------------
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: MigrationRequest
session_id: sess-01AF3C
source_node: node-12
target_node: node-99
mode: move
checkpoint: s3://session-checkpoints/prod/2026-03-30/sess-01AF3C.chk
priority: enterprise
notes: "drain by controller: node maintenance 2026-03-30T22:00Z"
---
